task_title: Review an unsafe production DB migration
output:
Disposition: request changes — do not run this inline on live heartbeat_runs.

(1) Locks: ALTER ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE—blocks all reads/writes, so heartbeat INSERTs stop for the lock duration (PG11+ is metadata-fast for constant DEFAULT but still exclusive). CREATE INDEX (non-CONCURRENT) takes SHARE, which conflicts with writers' ROW EXCLUSIVE—blocks INSERTs for the whole 40M build. UPDATE takes ROW EXCLUSIVE + row locks; alone it does not block other writers, but I/O/WAL storm starves the path.

(2) One migration txn + 40M-row UPDATE holds one snapshot for hours, huge WAL, frozen xmin (no VACUUM), timeout/OOM risk, full rollback on failure.

(3) Safe: ADD COLUMN cost_cents int NULL (commit); batched UPDATEs by id ranges with per-batch COMMIT + app dual-write; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (not in a txn); then SET DEFAULT 0 and SET NOT NULL only when no nulls remain.

judgeDetail.rationale: Nails all three hazards with correct lock modes (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, SHARE vs ROW EXCLUSIVE), notes PG11+ constant-default is metadata-fast, and gives batched backfill + CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, though it omits the NOT VALID/VALIDATE constraint technique (using SET NOT NULL, which itself briefly locks).
